messages.subject: NaN in DIC
parts:
Hi there,

I'm fitting several glm models with binomial response.
It turns out that the ones with a spatial spde model give NaNs in the DIC.
Looking closer, I can see that also p.eff, and mean.deviance are NaN,
while deviance.mean is a number.
A bunch of the local dic and p.eff are also NaNs.

But I don't understand why.

I have tried to reproduce the problem with a manufactured dataset, but
without success.
It works well.

Any clue?

Thanks!

Hi Havard,

Let me ask a couple of questions on this problem:

1. The example you added in the FAQ does not get NaN in DIC.
How can we 'detect' that there is a problem, then?
Only by looking at the posterior precision for the iid term?

2. In my dataset, the simple model Y ~ 1 + f(spatial, model=spde) still 
gets NaN in DIC.
Although now there is borrowing of strength.
Might it be suffering from the same problem, yet?
I looked at the hyperparameters but seem to be well identified, although 
K.0 gets negative values. Is this ok? Actually I don't know what T.0 and 
K.0 are.

Thank you for helping me understand what's going on.
        ƒacu.-



El 20/09/11 16:35, Håvard Rue escribió:
> On Tue, 2011-09-20 at 14:30 -0400, Facundo Muñoz wrote:
>> I had to control.fixed= list(prec.intercept = 1), in order to avoid
>> numerical problems.
>> Regarding the spde model, I used inla.spde.create(mesh, model="matern",
>> param=list(alpha=2)).
>>
>> How can I impose a lower range? As I understand, the parameter alpha is
>> related with the smoothness, but not the range.
>>
>> Here I send you the inla.model directory.
>>
>> I'm in the US right now.
>
> the problem is that you have binary data, and for each datapoint you
> have an iid random effect (U). this a case inla cannot handle really, as
> there is no replications and the loglikelihood is essentially flat. so
> you're asking to much from your data. try to remove 'U' and check if its
> improve, or, fix the precision for U.
>
>

> 2. In my dataset, the simple model Y ~ 1 + f(spatial, model=spde) still
> gets NaN in DIC.
> Although now there is borrowing of strength.
> Might it be suffering from the same problem, yet?
> I looked at the hyperparameters but seem to be well identified, although

you shouldn't really. can you send me the data and R so I can rerun it
here?

as you say, it might suffereing from the same problem, as NaN comes from
overflow in the numerics.

K.0 defines the \kappa^2 parameter as \log\kappa^2 = K.0, while \log
\prec=\T.0, in the SPDE.

There is a new interface to the SPDE stuff coming up (Finn is working on
it), which is called spde2, where the parametersiation will be much more
transparent and more general.

Best
